qt: to the Commission Vicent Marzà Ibáñez (Verts/ALE), Jaume Asens Llodrà (Verts/ALE), Estrella Galán (The Left) Subject:

For decades, the Commission has pursued the liberalisation of the rail sector through successive legislative packages and acts, including Directive 2012/34/EU and the fourth railway package – Directive (EU) 2016/2370 and Regulation (EU) 2016/2338. In doing so, it has fuelled competition, privatisation and the fragmentation of an essential public service. The accidents in Adamuz and Urda (Spain, 2026), Tempi (Greece, 2023) and Pardubice (Czechia, 2024), together with the progressive deterioration of railways in countries such as Germany and Belgium, call that model into question. Following decades of privatisation, the United Kingdom is bringing its railways back under public management. In this context, a proposal has been put forward in Spain to tackle the consequences of privatisation and fragmentation by reunifying the rail operator Renfe and the infrastructure manager Adif, carrying out an audit of the infrastructure, reversing outsourcing and bolstering staffing levels through increased public investment. 1.

Does the Commission accept responsibility for the consequences of its privatisation model for safety, maintenance, employment and service quality, and does it intend to carry out an independent assessment?

Will it revise the fourth railway package to remove competition requirements and press for renationalisation, the reunification of railway management and the restoration of railways as a public service?
What measures will it take to ensure that safety, labour rights and the social and environmental role of railways take precedence over private profitability criteria?
